The '''2021–22 season''' was the [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|120th season]] in the existence of [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City Football Club]] and their 20th consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2021–22 Premier League|domestic league]], Manchester City also participated in this season's editions of the [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2021 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] and [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

The club kicked off the season by losing the Community Shield to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and was later knocked out of the EFL Cup by [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the fourth round, ending their unbeaten streak in the competition that had stretched to nearly five years. City also reached the FA Cup semi-finals for the fifth time in Guardiola's six-season tenure, but were beaten by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], the Blues' third consecutive semi-final defeat. In Europe, City were coming off their most successful [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] campaign in history and looked to improve on last season's [[2021 UEFA Champions League final|final]] loss to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. They reached the semi-finals again, but were defeated there by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] 6–5 on aggregate [[Overtime (sports)#Association football)|after extra time]] over the two closely fought and very dramatic games. On a brighter note, City successfully retained the Premier League title in another intense title race with Liverpool. This was the second time the Blues managed to defend the trophy (both under [[Pep Guardiola]]) and their fourth title in five years. City secured the league title by a single point on the final matchday with a dramatic 3–2 comeback victory over [[2021–22 Aston Villa F.C. season|Aston Villa]]. The second-half turnaround bore striking similarities to City's [[Manchester City F.C. 3–2 Queens Park Rangers F.C.|title-clinching game]] from the [[2011–12 Premier League|2011–12 Premier League season]], exactly ten seasons earlier.

The season was Manchester City's first since [[2010–11 Manchester City F.C. season|2010–11]] not to feature their [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Goalscorers|all-time record goalscorer]] [[Sergio Agüero]], who had left the club for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on a free transfer at the end of the previous season; he went on to retire from football following cardiac health problems in November 2021. City were unable to immediately recruit a like-for-like replacement for Agüero, and this season was notable for Guardiola's extensive use of a [[Forward (association football)#False 9|false 9]] role. Agüero's departure proved to be no impediment to the Blues scoring 150 goals in all competitions, the most of any senior top-tier professional team in Europe; they were closely followed by Liverpool with 147 goals, although [[Jürgen Klopp]]'s side played six more matches.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bray |first=Joe |date=2022-05-29 |title=Liverpool's Champions League final blank hands Man City another record |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-city-goals-liverpool-madrid-24091626 |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en}}</ref>

==Season summary==
===Pre-season===
[[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]] began with 15 Manchester City first team players selected in the qualified [[UEFA Euro 2020 squads|squads]], which was the joint-most representatives from a single club (shared with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]).<ref>{{cite web|date=2021-06-05|title=Top 10 clubs with the most players participating in EURO 2020|url=https://technosports.co.in/2021/06/05/top-10-clubs-with-the-most-players-participating-in-euro-2020/|access-date=2021-08-01|website=TechnoSports|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Host of Premier League stars in action at Euro 2020|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2163392|access-date=2021-08-01|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> However, [[João Cancelo|Joao Cancelo]] was forced to withdraw days after the tournament began due to a positive [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS‑CoV‑2]] test result,<ref>{{cite web|date=2021-06-13|title=Cancelo to miss Euro 2020, Dalot called up|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/portugal-por/story/4407155/man-citys-joao-cancelo-to-miss-euro-2020-due-to-covid-portugal-call-up-diogo-dalot|access-date=2021-08-01|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> and [[Eric García (footballer, born 2001)|Eric Garcia]] joined [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] while the tournament was in progress. Out of these City players, all their squads reached the [[UEFA Euro 2020 knockout phase|knock-out stages]], seven reached the semi-finals and four [[England national football team|England]] players reached the [[UEFA Euro 2020 Final|final]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Clayton|first=David|title=City quartet help create history as England book place in Euro 2020 final|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/england-v-denmark-manchester-city-angle-match-report-63761284|access-date=2021-08-01|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref> but ended up as runners-up.

City also had [[2021 Copa América squads|three representatives]] selected at the [[2021 Copa América]], [[Sergio Agüero]] joining Barcelona while the tournament was in progress. All three reached the [[2021 Copa América Final|final]], but the two remaining [[Brazil national football team|Brazilian]] players ended up as runners-up.<ref>{{cite web|last=Oatway|first=Caroline|title=Heartbreak for Brazil in Copa America Final|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/copa-america-brazil-ederson-final-63761589|access-date=2021-08-01|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

As a result of having many players involved deep into these tournaments and with City's involvement in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|2021 Champions League final]], City began their pre-season with all but eight of their first team rested on holiday. Only [[Zack Steffen]], [[Benjamin Mendy]], [[Riyad Mahrez]] and [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandinho]] from the regular starters in [[2020–21 Manchester City F.C. season|2020–21]] were able to participate in a full pre-season. However, this gave an opportunity for several [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|EDS]] players to showcase their talents for a possible first team place.

Most of the pre-season transfer speculation concerned the potential replacements for Sergio Agüero, who had left at the end of the 2020–21 season after 10 years and as the club's [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Goalscorers|all-time leading goalscorer]]. Of the potential targets, [[Harry Kane]] was seen as the leading candidate, but was expected to command a significant and possibly record-breaking [[Transfer (association football)|transfer fee]] from [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]].<ref>{{cite web|date=2021-06-21|title=Manchester City make Harry Kane bid worth at least £100m to Tottenham|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jun/21/manchester-city-harry-kane-bid-worth-at-least-100m-to-tottenham-reject|access-date=2021-08-01|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> There was also speculation that [[Jack Grealish]] would be signed from [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on a similarly record fee to strengthen City's creative [[Midfielder|midfield]] and provide additional cover for [[Kevin De Bruyne]], who had experienced several extended periods of injury absence during the previous seasons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jack Grealish: Manchester City's £100m transfer bid for England midfielder expected to be accepted by Aston Villa|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11677/12368063/jack-grealish-manchester-citys-100m-transfer-bid-for-england-midfielder-expected-to-be-accepted-by-aston-villa|access-date=2021-08-01|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin de Bruyne - latest news, stats, injury updates and contract|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/kevin-de-bruyne|access-date=2021-08-01|website=www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk}}</ref>

Grealish completed his transfer to City on 5 August 2021, signing a 6-year contract, for what at the time was a reported [[List of most expensive association football transfers#Highest transfer records in association football|record British transfer fee]] of £100 million.<ref name=":0" /> He was allocated the iconic number 10 shirt, previously worn by Agüero between 2015 and 2021.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Grealish squad number revealed|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/jack-grealish-man-city-squad-number-63763785|access-date=2021-08-05|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Start of season===
On 7 August, Manchester City started their season with the [[2021 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]], a traditional curtain raiser played between the previous season's [[2020–21 Premier League|league champions]] and [[2021 FA Cup Final|FA Cup winners]]. This was City's first FA Community Shield since [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019]] when they beat [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 5–4 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] after a 1–1 draw. On this occasion, an understrength City (many players were still out-of-form after Euro 2020) were beaten 1–0 at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] with an 89th-minute penalty won and scored by former City academy graduate [[Kelechi Iheanacho]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Leicester beat Man City to win Community Shield|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58036460|access-date=2021-08-15}}</ref>

The [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League season]] began with all restrictions on stadium attendances lifted for the first time since the start of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|pandemic]] in March 2020.<ref>{{cite web|number=161385360554578|date=2021-08-10|title=Fans allowed back? Stadium capacity info for 2021/22 Premier League season|url=https://talksport.com/football/922668/fans-allowed-back-stadium-capacity-premier-league-2021-22-season/|access-date=2021-08-15|website=talkSPORT|language=en-US}}</ref>

City began their league season on 15 August with a third consecutive competitive 1–0 defeat, this time against Tottenham at their north London [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium|stadium]]. This was the first time in 10 years that City had failed to win their opening league game of the season; coincidentally the last time being a 0–0 away draw at [[White Hart Lane]] in the [[2010–11 Manchester City F.C. season|2010–11]] season. It was also City's fourth consecutive defeat at Tottenham since the new stadium was opened and meant that City had yet to score a goal at this ground.

On 25 August, Harry Kane announced he would be staying at Tottenham "this summer", ending the speculation that City would be able to negotiate an acceptable transfer fee with Tottenham's chairman [[Daniel Levy (businessman)|Daniel Levy]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Kane says he is staying at Spurs|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58331546|access-date=2021-08-26}}</ref> On the same day it was reported that Pep Guardiola had revealed that he would leave the club when his current contract ends in summer 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Guardiola plans to leave Man City in 2023|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58339343|access-date=2021-08-26}}</ref> However, Guardiola later retracted this and said he was talking about whenever his contract at City ended he would be considering an opportunity to manage a national side.

On 26 August, [[Benjamin Mendy]] was charged by [[Cheshire Constabulary]] with four counts of [[rape]] and one count of [[sexual assault]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Baynes |first=Megan |url=https://news.sky.com/story/manchester-city-footballer-benjamin-mendy-charged-with-four-counts-of-rape-12391379 |title=Manchester City footballer Benjamin Mendy charged with four counts of rape |date=26 August 2021 |access-date=26 August 2021 |work=[[Sky News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-manchester-58348288 |title=Benjamin Mendy: Manchester City footballer charged with rape |work=[[BBC News]] |date=26 August 2021 |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref> Mendy was immediately suspended by City and remanded in custody with a trial date set for 24 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-manchester-58516300|title=Benjamin Mendy: Manchester City footballer in court on rape charges|work=BBC News|date=10 September 2021}}</ref> This was later set back until June 2022.

On 8 September, it was announced that Brazil and three other [[South America]]n nations had invoked a five-day [[FIFA]] ban on Premier League players who had been called up for international duty for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2022 World Cup qualifiers]] during the September international window, but who had been refused permission to travel by their clubs to avoid a 10-day [[quarantine]] period required by [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK Government]] public health regulations when they returned from so-called "[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|Red list]]" countries with high levels of [[COVID-19]] infection. This would have prevented City from including [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] and [[Gabriel Jesus]] in their squad to play Leicester City on 11 September.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Premier League will not release players|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58322829|access-date=2021-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=PL clubs hope players will be free to play|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58486811|access-date=2021-09-09}}</ref> However, the ban was rescinded on the morning of the fixture, and City went on to win the game 1–0 with both Brazilian players in the starting XI.<ref>{{Cite news|title=England-based players avoid bans|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58522907|access-date=2021-09-11}}</ref>

On 15 September, City beat [[RB Leipzig]] 6–3 in their first [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group A|group game]] of the season. At the time, this was Pep Guardiola's 300th game as City manager and 750th overall. The Blues became the fastest English team to register 50 Champions League wins (in 91 games) and the second fastest of all time behind [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (88 games).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=City become fastest English team to register 50 Champions League wins|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-50-champions-league-wins-63767329|access-date=2021-09-16|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>{{efn|These 50 UCL wins exclude two victories over [[FC Steaua București]] in the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round#Play-off round|2016–17 qualifying play-off round]].}}

===Autumn period===
On 21 September, City beat [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] 6–1 at home in the third round of the [[2021–22 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]]. This win was Pep Guardiola's 220th as City manager, equalling the club record previously held by [[Les McDowall|Les McDowell]] between 1950 and 1963. Guardiola had achieved this in only 302 games compared to 592 games managed by McDowell. The game was also noteworthy in that six academy graduates made their City first team debuts that night, the most in the modern history of the club academy.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=Barry-Murphy: Academy debuts a proud moment for us all|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/eds-academy/brian-barry-murphy-on-academy-pride-at-eds-city-debuts-63767906|access-date=2021-09-23|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 25 September, City defeated Chelsea, one of their main title rivals, who at the time were on a streak of three consecutive wins against City, including in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]]. The Blues recorded a 1–0 away win at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] to mark Guardiola's 221st City win and make him the most successful manager in the club's history.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Guardiola sets new club record after Chelsea win|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-most-wins-manchester-city-63768173|access-date=2021-09-25|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 12 October, five City players started for England versus [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] in their [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)#Group I|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifier]] 1–1 draw at [[Wembley Stadium]]. This set a new club record for representatives starting in a national team XI.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Clayton|first=David|title=New Club record as five City players start for England|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/new-england-record-for-manchester-city-players-63769663|access-date=2021-10-13|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 27 October, City were beaten 5–3 on penalties after a goalless draw at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup, thus ending their 4-year domination of the competition, in which they had not lost a competitive fixture in 21 games since the [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season#EFL Cup|2016–17 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Edwards|first=John|title=City bow out of Carabao Cup on penalties|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/west-ham-manchester-city-carabao-cup-match-report-63770955|access-date=2021-10-27|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

City's early season league form was variable, and by the time of the final autumn [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]] in early November they had two defeats and two draws from their first 11 league fixtures and only two points more than in the [[2020–21 Manchester City F.C. season|2020–21]] season (where they had also started off slowly, but then had embarked on a record-breaking mid season winning streak to secure their league title). However, City had by then played all of the [[2020–21 Premier League|previous season]]'s other top 5 clubs away from home, remaining undefeated and only dropping points in their 2–2 draw against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]]. The other favourites for the league title had also dropped points; so that by 7 November City were in second place, just 3 points behind the early league leaders Chelsea, and equal on points with surprise form team [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]]. With 2 group games remaining City were also just a point from qualifying for the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout stage]] of that season's Champions League.

On 24 November, City duly qualified for the last 16 of the Champions League as Group A winners when they beat [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint Germain]] 2–1 at home.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man City beat PSG to seal top spot|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59392458|access-date=2021-11-24}}</ref>

City's 2–1 away victory against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 1 December was Guardiola's 150th win in the Premier League. He became only the 4th manager to achieve this at a single club and the fastest to achieve the milestone (in only 204 games).<ref>{{cite news|title=Sensational Sterling impresses as Guardiola clocks up 150th PL win|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-post-match-reaction-villa-1-2-man-city-63773995|work=mancity.com|access-date=2021-12-01}}</ref>

On 4 December (gameweek 15), City beat Watford 3–1 away to notch up 5 consecutive league victories and reach the top of the Premier League for the first time that season.

City's 1–0 win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]] in their following league game was notable as [[Raheem Sterling]] scored his [[List of footballers with 100 or more Premier League goals|100th Premier League goal]] and [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] kept his 100th [[Shutout#Association football|clean sheet]] for the club in all competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Sterling joins Premier League 100 club with goal v Wolves|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/raheem-sterling-100-premier-league-goals-63774828|access-date=2021-12-11|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Ederson clocks up a century of City clean sheets|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/ederson-100-manchester-city-clean-sheets-63774829|access-date=2021-12-11|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Christmas and New Year===
[[File:2021-12-07 Fußball, Männer, UEFA Champions League, RB Leipzig - Manchester City FC 1DX 2558 by Stepro.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Kevin De Bruyne]] and [[Riyad Mahrez]] in an away [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match against [[RB Leipzig|Leipzig]]]]

On 14 December, City beat [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] 7–0 at home to record their biggest victory of the season so far. The first goal, scored by [[Phil Foden]], marked the 500th scored by a Pep Guardiola team in the Premier League; he became the fastest to record this feat after only 207 games, beating the previous record by [[Jürgen Klopp|Jurgen Klopp]] (234 games).<ref>{{cite news|title=Man City 7-0 Leeds: Premier League leaders go four points clear after attacking masterclass|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59558240|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> This win also was City's 33rd league victory of the calendar year, equalling a top flight record set by Liverpool in [[1982–83 Liverpool F.C. season|1982]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Edwards|first=John|title=Victory over Leeds wins LMA Performance of the Week|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/lma-performance-of-the-week-city-leeds-united-63775337|access-date=2021-12-17|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 19 December, City's 4–0 win away to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]] ensured they would stay top of the table at Christmas. It also signified two new records: for the most league wins by an English top flight team in a calendar year (34) and for the most league goals scored in a calendar year by a Premier League team (106), despite still having two league games to play before the New Year.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Clayton|first=David|title=Record-breaking City cruise to victory over Newcastle|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/newcastle-united-v-manchester-city-match-report-19-dec-63775518|access-date=2021-12-19|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 28 December, City announced that Spanish forward [[Ferran Torres]] would join Barcelona in the New Year for a reported fee of €55m (£46.3m) upfront and up to €10m (£9.3m) in possible add-ons. Torres had not played for City since the League Cup victory against Wycombe in late September due to an injury picked up during the October internationals. He had been at the club for only 18 months, but City had recouped over double his transfer fee from [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref name=":3" /> Barcelona needed a forward to replace Sergio Agüero who had been forced to retire early on medical grounds a few weeks beforehand.

City maintained their ten-game league winning streak into the New Year. They ended 2021 with 50 points, eight points clear of Chelsea at the top of the table and nine points ahead of Liverpool in third place, who also had a game in hand. In all, City had won 36 league games in 2021 and scored 113 goals, setting new [[Football records and statistics in England#League|top division]] and [[Premier League records and statistics|Premier League records]] respectively.

Another close fought game against Chelsea, this time at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]], was won 1–0 on 15 January thanks to a beautiful [[Kevin De Bruyne]] curling shot, producing a statement victory for the Blues and extending their league winning run to 12 games. The result put City on 56 points, 13 ahead of Chelsea in second and 14 ahead of Liverpool in third, who still had two games in hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/15/manchester-city-chelsea-premier-league-match-report|title=Kevin De Bruyne fires Manchester City 13 points clear of toothless Chelsea|author=David Hytner|work=The Guardian|date=15 January 2022|access-date=20 January 2022}}</ref>

However, City's winning streak was ended in the following game on 22 January when they drew 1–1 away to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and their league lead was cut to nine points from Liverpool, who still had a game in hand. However, the result signified another new record as Guardiola became the fastest manager to reach 500 Premier League points earned, in only 213 games – eighteen games fewer than his closest rival.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Guardiola becomes fastest manager to reach 500 Premier League points|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-500-premier-league-points-63778476|access-date=2022-01-23|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On winter transfer deadline day, City announced that they had signed 22 year-old Argentine versatile forward [[Julián Álvarez (footballer)|Julián Álvarez]] for a reported £14.1 million fee from [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]. Álvarez had subsequently been loaned back to River Plate until at least July 2022 so that he would be able to participate in the [[2022 Copa Libertadores]] for his previous club. If River Plate qualified to the quarter-finals or beyond his loan might be extended as far as the break for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]]. At the time, Álvarez was the current [[South American Footballer of the Year]] and the golden boot holder for the [[Argentine Primera Division]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester City sign Julian Alvarez from River Plate|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60189980|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=1 February 2022}}</ref>

===Spring period===
Raheem Sterling scored City's first [[hat-trick]] of the season in their 4–0 win away to [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] in the Premier League on 12 February 2022. It was notable as a perfect hat-trick, and took Sterling onto the list of top 10 [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#All-time top goalscorers|goal-scorers]] in all competitions for the club .<ref name=":4" />

City earnt a commanding first leg lead in their Champions League round of 16 tie against [[Sporting CP]], beating the [[2021–22 Primeira Liga|Portuguese champions]] 5–0 away on 15 February, including a [[Hat-trick|brace]] from [[Bernardo Silva]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=UEFA.com|title=Sporting CP-Man. City {{!}} UEFA Champions League|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2033897--sporting-cp-vs-man-city/|access-date=2022-02-20|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref>

However, they went on to be beaten 3–2 at home by [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Spurs]] in their next league fixture; their first league defeat for four months; and a result which closed the gap at the top of the table to second placed Liverpool to only 6 points, with Liverpool still having a game in hand and still to play City at the City of Manchester Stadium in early April. City had equalised twice in the game, including a 92nd-minute penalty from [[Riyad Mahrez]] (which was notable as City's 100th goal in all competitions that season), but the game was won by a headed goal in the 95th minute from erstwhile City transfer target [[Harry Kane]], who had already scored Spurs second goal earlier in the second half.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Kane gives Tottenham dramatic late win over Man City|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60357463|access-date=2022-02-20}}</ref>

[[File:Manchester United v Manchester City, 6 November 2021 (07).jpg|thumb|right|200px|City players celebrate during the [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League]] game against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]]]

An outstanding team performance against their closest rivals saw City convincingly beat Manchester United 4–1 at home on 6 March with a brace apiece from Riyad Mahrez and man of the match Kevin De Bruyne. This broke a sequence of 3 consecutive derby losses at home. Mahrez had now scored over 20 goals in a season in all competitions for the first time in his career and De Bruyne passed the milestone of fifty Premier League goals. The result still meant City led the league from Liverpool by 6 points having played a game more.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Man City v Man Utd, 2021/22 {{!}} Premier League |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66616 |access-date=2022-03-06 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>

City drew 0–0 with Sporting on 9 March in the second leg of their Champions League round of 16 tie to win 5–0 on aggregate and qualify for the quarter-finals for the fifth season in succession.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City comfortably into quarter-finals |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60666631 |access-date=2022-03-09}}</ref> By the time of the March international break, City's lead in the league had been cut to 1 point after another frustrating 0–0 draw with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at [[Selhurst Park]] on 14 March and Liverpool's continued league winning streak since January.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Palace hold wasteful Man City in draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60642772 |access-date=2022-03-15}}</ref> On a brighter note, the Blues qualified for their fourth consecutive FA Cup semi-final when they beat [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 4–1 at [[St Mary's Stadium|St. Mary's]] on 20 March.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City see off Saints to reach semis |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60698116 |access-date=2022-03-20}}</ref>

===Season run-in===
City returned from the March international break knowing they had up to 16 games of the season remaining over eight weeks, in which they could secure a [[Treble (association football)|treble]] of titles. This would start with a sequence of five games over 14 days where the Blues would play both Atlético Madrid and Liverpool twice in alternating fixtures: the two-legged Champions League quarter-finals, a potentially decisive home league fixture and a FA Cup semi-final at Wembley.

However, first City had to retake the top spot from Liverpool, which they successfully accomplished by beating [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] 2–0 at [[Turf Moor]] on 2 April, after their rivals had defeated [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] by the same score at home earlier that day. Three days later, a 1–0 victory over Atlético in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals gave City a slender advantage before heading to Madrid. On 10 April, an exciting and high quality 2–2 home draw against Liverpool ensured City retained a single point advantage at the top of the league with seven games remaining.

Just three days after a title decider versus Liverpool, City faced Atlético on the road. An intense and maturely hard fought 0–0 draw in Madrid ensured City progressed to the semi-finals for the second consecutive season. There, the Blues would face [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] who had closely beaten Chelsea over the two legs. Unfortunately, the closeness of the Atlético tie prevented Guardiola from resting his strongest squad, and several key players suffered injuries while [[Jürgen Klopp]] was able to effectively play his "B team" in Liverpool's quarter-final home tie against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] the same night.

The FA Cup semi-final awaited in just three days, on 16 April, after an excruciating battle with Atlético. As such, Guardiola was forced to make seven changes for the match against Liverpool. A dominant display from the Scoursers at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] saw them take a three-goal lead against an underperforming City side by half-time, including a [[Sadio Mané]] goal which resulted from an error from back up keeper [[Zack Steffen]], who Guardiola always selected to play in City's domestic cup fixtures. The Blues managed to improve in the second half, with goals from Jack Grealish and Bernardo Silva nearly erasing the deficit, but Liverpool withstood the pressure to a nervous 3–2 victory, ending Citizens' hopes of the treble. Although Manchester City had reached five [[FA Cup semi-finals]] during Guardiola's tenure at the club, they had only succeeded in reaching one final (in [[2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season#FA Cup|2019]]), while losing three consecutive FA Cup semi-finals starting from [[2019–20 Manchester City F.C. season#FA Cup|2020]] and also losing three consecutive appearances at Wembley.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Liverpool beat Man City to reach FA Cup final |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61120882 |access-date=2022-04-17}}</ref>

A 3–0 win against [[Brighton and Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] on 20 April saw City keep Liverpool at the same distance of a point. This victory was Guardiola's 250th as City manager in all competitions. Just three days later, the Blues produced another convincing win, this time beating [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] 5–1. [[Gabriel Jesus]] scored four goals and became the third City player to do so in a Premier League match after Sergio Agüero and [[Edin Džeko]]. This was also City's 15th consecutive Premier League victory against the Hornets, setting another PL record.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jesus scores four as City beat Watford to keep Premier league lead|url=https://mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-watford-premier-league-match-report-63786322|publisher=mancity.com|access-date=25 April 2022}}</ref>

Another three days later, on 26 April, Manchester City defeated Real Madrid 4–3 in an outstanding game at a capacity City of Manchester Stadium to take a slight advantage to the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]]. City scored in under two minutes, as Kevin De Bruyne finished the fastest goal in European Cup semi-finals history, and had held a two-goal advantage on three occasions during the match, while also squandering multiple good opportunities to increase the lead, only to see a resilient Madrid side reduce the deficit to a single goal, courtesy of a brace (which included a [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka]] penalty) from Real Madrid's top scorer, captain and talisman [[Karim Benzema]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Man. City-Real Madrid {{!}} UEFA Champions League 2021/22 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2034662/ |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref> The match was also notable by numerous missed goal opportunities (hitting the post, goal line clearances, goalkeeper saves) on the part of City players, with observers commenting that a 7–3 scoreline would have been more fair.<ref>[https://twitter.com/castilloerling9/status/1648423212248858625?s=46&t=jtNjdZ6HsfB6xfJ3b_ZTMA Man City-Real Madrid]</ref>

In their next league game, City beat [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds]] away 4–0 to keep a one-point lead over Liverpool with just four PL games remaining. City had not conceded a league goal away from home in five consecutive fixtures and had remained undefeated in 16 away league games since their opening day loss at Tottenham (both new club records). Captain [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandihno]] came on as a substitute to become the [[Brazilian Football Confederation|Brazilian]] player with the most Premier League [[List of foreign Premier League players#Brazil|appearances]] and celebrated by scoring City's final goal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clayton |first=David |title=City return to summit after stern Leeds test |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/leeds-united-v-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report-30-april-63786930 |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=www.mancity.com |language=en}}</ref>

===End of season===
4 May was a tough day for the Blues, as they failed to reach the [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] in the most dramatic and heartbreaking fashion at the Santiago Bernabéu. Leading the game 1–0 (5–3 on aggregate), from a 75th-minute goal by [[Riyad Mahrez]], City once again squandered several opportunities to put the game to bed and collapsed in the last minutes of the match. Approaching the injury time, it appeared City were heading comfortably to the final, where they would have met rivals Liverpool; however, two goals in a minute from Madrid's [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] striker [[Rodrygo]] sent the game into [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]], and another penalty from Benzema five minutes later proved to be the winner as City were defeated 1–3 (5–6 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=City suffer Champions League heartbreak against Real Madrid|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/real-madrid-v-manchester-city-champions-league-semi-final-63787297|access-date=2022-05-10|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

The heartbreak, however, did not derail City as some rivals might have hoped. By the time of City's next league game on 8 May, Liverpool had finally dropped points in the title race by drawing 1–1 against Tottenham at Anfield.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool v Spurs, 2021/22 {{!}} Premier League |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66699 |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> City were able to put their shock and disappointment from the Bernabéu to one side and capitalise on this, opening up a three-point lead and a four-goal difference advantage after a 5–0 thrashing of revitalised [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] with a brace from Raheem Sterling and another man of the match performance from Kevin De Bruyne. The Blues required seven more points from three remaining fixtures to secure and retain their league title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clayton |first=David |title=Super City go three points clear after Newcastle rout |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-v-newcastle-united-premier-league-match-report-8-may-2022-63787619 |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=www.mancity.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 May, the club officially announced it had reached agreement with [[Borussia Dortmund]] to sign young [[Norway national football team|Norwegian]] striker [[Erling Haaland]] on 1 July 2022 subject to completing terms. Haaland, the son of ex-City and Leeds midfielder [[Alf-Inge Haaland]], was one of the most sought-after players in world football, having scored 85 goals in 88 appearances for Dortmund, and became the heir-apparent to Sergio Agüero the club had been seeking for several years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pollard |first=Rob |title=Club statement on Erling Haaland |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/club-statement-erling-haaland-63787789 |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=www.mancity.com |language=en}}</ref>

Another big 5–1 win away at [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]] on 11 May, including four goals from Kevin De Bruyne, and a 24-minute hat-trick (the third fastest from the start of a game in Premier League history), reduced City's target to getting a maximum of four points from two remaining fixtures to retain their title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clayton |first=David |title=Magnificent four-goal De Bruyne destroys Wolves |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/wolves-v-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report-63787892 |access-date=2022-05-11 |website=www.mancity.com |language=en}}</ref> This game was Guardiola's 350th as City manager. It also signified another Premier League record for consecutive games won by a margin of three or more goals.

On 15 May, City fought back from conceding two first-half goals to draw 2–2 at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]], and could have won the match but for a late penalty miss from  Riyad Mahrez. This was the first time since 2012 that City had come back from a two-goal deficit in a game. Nevertheless, the result still meant the Blues would win the league if they won their final fixture at home versus Aston Villa.

The season ended in dramatic circumstances on 22 May, as City once again overturned a two-goal deficit. With 15 minutes left to play, the Blues scored three goals in five minutes, including a brace from [[İlkay Gündoğan]], to beat Aston Villa 3–2 and clinch the Premier League title amid jubilant scenes at the City of Manchester Stadium. Manchester City finished the league season on 93 points, one more than rivals Liverpool, making it their second consecutive league title and repeating the scenario of the [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12616090/man-city-3-2-aston-villa-premier-league-title-won-in-dramatic-fashion-as-city-come-from-two-down-to-win-late-on|title=Man City champions after incredible turnaround|date=23 May 2022|access-date=23 May 2022|author=Adam Bate|website=[[Sky Sports]]|language=en}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 14 July, City announced they would host [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] at the [[Academy Stadium]] on 27 July,<ref>{{cite web |title=City To Host Preston North End In Pre-Season Friendly |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/preston-pre-season-friendly-63761854 |publisher=Manchester City FC |access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref> and would travel to [[France]] to take on fellow [[City Football Group|CFG]] club [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]] on 31 July.<ref>{{cite web |title=City Travel To Troyes For All-CFG Pre-Season Friendly |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-friendly-cfg-es-troyes-ac-63761876 |publisher=Manchester City FC |access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref> The Troyes game was later postponed indefinitely due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in France|COVID-19 restrictions in France]] and [[COVID-19 pandemic in England|England]]. Had the match taken place, City would have had to quarantine and therefore miss their [[2021 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] match against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. It was replaced by a game against Barnsley on 31 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/manchestercity/news/manchester-city-will-play-barnsley-fc-in-their-second-pre-season-friendly-at-the-academy-stadium-on-saturday-evening|title=Man City To Play Barnsley In Second Pre-Season Friendly|website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> The same day, City's final preseason friendly against [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] was announced and scheduled for 3 August.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/blackpool-fc/blackpool-to-take-on-premier-league-champions-man-city-in-final-pre-season-friendly-before-bristol-city-opener-3330326|title=Blackpool to take on Premier League champions Man City in final pre-season friendly before Bristol City opener|website=www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk|date=31 July 2021 }}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2021–22 FA Cup}}
As a Premier League club, City entered the tournament in the third round proper. The third round draw was held on 6 December 2021 live on [[ITV4]], before the second round tie between [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]] and [[St Albans City F.C.|St. Albans City]], by former England internationals [[David Seaman]] and [[Faye White]]. City were drawn away to [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Emirates FA Cup third round proper draw was made on Monday evening|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2021/dec/06/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-20210612|date=6 December 2021|access-date=7 December 2021|publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> The draw for the fourth round took place live on [[ITV (TV network)|ITV]] ahead of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s visit to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], with former City goalkeeper [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]] and current [[Arsenal W.F.C.|Arsenal Women]] captain [[Leah Williamson]] picking out the ties at Wembley Stadium. City were drawn out at home against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite news|title=City learn FA Cup fourth round opponents|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-fa-cup-fourth-round-details-63777320|date=9 January 2022|access-date=11 January 2022|publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> The [[2021–22 FA Cup#Fifth round proper|fifth round]] draw was held on 5 February 2022 prior to the tie between [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on ITV by [[Andy Cole|Andrew Cole]]. City were drawn away to [[2021–22 EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]], who they had only played once before: on their way to the [[1980–81 FA Cup|1981]] FA Cup [[1981 FA Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-02-06|title=FA Cup draw: Prem big guns avoid each other|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-fa-cup/story/4587492/fa-cup-fifth-round-draw-luton-vs-chelseapeterborough-vs-man-city|access-date=2022-02-07|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> The quarter-final draw was held on 3 March 2022 prior to the tie between [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]] on ITV by [[England national football team|England]] manager [[Gareth Southgate]]. City were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Boro to host Chelsea in FA Cup quarters |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60609126 |access-date=2022-03-03}}</ref> The semi-final draw was made by [[Robbie Fowler]] at [[City Ground|the City Ground]] on ITV before the quarter-final between [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and Liverpool. City were drawn against the winner of that tie, who turned out to be Liverpool after a hard-fought 1–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FA Cup semi-final draw: Man City to face Nottingham Forest or Liverpool as Chelsea take on Crystal Palace |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12571447/fa-cup-semi-final-draw-man-city-to-face-nottingham-forest-or-liverpool-as-chelsea-take-on-crystal-palace |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2021–22 EFL Cup}}
The draw for the third round was made on 25 August 2021 live on [[Sky Sports]] after the conclusion of the second round tie between [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and Arsenal by [[Kevin Phillips (footballer)|Kevin Phillips]] and [[Kevin Campbell (footballer)|Kevin Campbell]]. City were drawn at home versus League One side [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup Round Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2021/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw-confirmed/ |publisher=EFL |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date Confirmed For Wycombe Cup Clash |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-wycombe-wanderers-carabao-cup-date-set-63766097 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> The draw for the fourth round was made on 22 September 2021 after the conclusion of the third round ties by [[Micah Richards]] and [[Harry Redknapp]]. City were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], who had beaten [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]] in the third round.<ref>{{cite news|title=Carabao Cup: Holders Man City to face West Ham in fourth round, Arsenal host Leeds United, Liverpool visit Preston|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12414738/carabao-cup-holders-manchester-city-to-face-west-ham-in-fourth-round|access-date=23 September 2021|publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date And Time Confirmed For West Ham Carabao Cup Clash |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/west-ham-v-manchester-city-carabao-cup-date-confirmed-63768074 |access-date=24 September 2021 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=24 September 2021}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2021–22 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}

=====Round of 16=====
The draw for the round of 16 was held on 13 December 2021 at UEFA's headquarters in [[Nyon]]. An administrative error led to a first draw being declared [[Void (law)|null and void]] after a series of errors, including some [[Seed (sports)#Association football|seeded]] teams being allowed into the draw with runners-up from their own qualification groups.<ref>{{cite news|title=UEFA declare Champions League draw void after series of errors|url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/manchester-united-handed-psg-tie-121848030.html|date=13 December 2021|access-date=13 December 2021|website=Yahoo Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Champions League round of 16 draw declared void and will be redone at 15:00 CET|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0270-13f2ac0aff13-74f2ff9e43b1-1000--champions-league-round-of-16-draw-declared-void-and-will-be-red/|date=13 December 2021|access-date=13 December 2021|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref> City had initially been drawn against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]]. The draw was subsequently redone three hours later and City were drawn against [[Sporting CP]],<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Champions League round of 16 draw|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/draws/2022/2001309/?_font=l&_img=|date=13 December 2021|access-date=13 December 2021|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref> who they had last met and lost on away goals to in the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Round of 16|last 16]] of the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]].

==Awards==
In the end of season awards, [[Kevin De Bruyne]] won [[Premier League Player of the Season]] for the second time,<ref name=":5">{{cite news |title=De Bruyne voted EA SPORTS Player of the Season |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2621844 |access-date=21 May 2022 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> and the club's own Player of the Season award for the fourth time, equalling the club record; [[Phil Foden]] won [[Premier League Young Player of the Season]] and the PFA Young Player of the Year, both for the second consecutive season;<ref name=":6">{{cite news |title=Foden named Hublot Young Player of the Season |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2621849 |access-date=21 May 2022 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{cite news |last=Leigh |first=Neil |title=Foden wins second PFA Young Player of the Year award |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/phil-foden-pfa-young-player-of-the-year-63790387 |access-date=9 June 2022 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> while [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] won the [[Premier League Golden Glove]] for the third consecutive season, this time sharing the award with Liverpool's first choice keeper [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]] (both were on 20 clean sheets). Three City players were also included in the PFA Team of the Year (Cancelo, De Bruyne and Silva).<ref name=":8">{{cite news |last=Edwards |first=John |title=City trio named in PFA Team of the Year |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pfa-team-of-the-year-202122-cancelo-de-bruyne-bernardo-63790387 |access-date=9 June 2022  |website=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref>
